claims.text: Entire pancake range is 米粉100% (100% rice flour); no wheat flour or wheat pasta is used on the premises, so batter-level cross-contact is inherently low. However no formal celiac cross-contact protocol is published.

Savory pancakes such as ハーブ鶏の照り焼き (herb-chicken teriyaki, described as 甘じょっぱい / sweet-salty) and the Shinshu salmon plate use teriyaki/soy-based sauces that are wheat unless tamari — a celiac should confirm the sauce or choose the sweet pancakes.
Whipped cream is soy-milk based (dairy-free) but pancake batter contains free-range egg, so pancakes are not vegan.
No published allergy/celiac handling protocol found; the shop markets 'gluten-free pancakes' but is not a certified celiac kitchen. Communicate celiac disease directly at ordering.

Concept is 100% rice flour with no wheat flour on premises, plus reduced sugar, soy-milk cream, organic local produce and Nagano red sorghum — a genuinely rice-flour-first kitchen, unusual on the Hakuba route.

name: Hibi Donut (日々どーなつ 松本中町店)

claims.text: Shop makes both 米粉 (wheat-free) and 小麦粉 (wheat) donuts in the same small kitchen; no dedicated GF fryer or line is stated by the venue, so cross-contact is plausible.
GF blogger warns: 「それ以外のドーナツは小麦を使用していますので、アレルギー表示を必ずご確認ください」 (other donuts use wheat — always check the allergen label) and does not confirm dedicated equipment.
No published allergen-handling protocol; blogger advises confirming allergen labels in person. Ask directly about separate frying oil for the 米粉 donuts.
The 米粉 old-fashioned donuts are made with in-house-milled rice flour and are described as 小麦粉不使用 (wheat-flour-free).

name: Jinenya Karuizawa Bypass (じねんや 軽井沢バイパス店)

claims.text: 「小麦粉を使ったメニューと、調理器具、食器を共用しているので、重篤な小麦アレルギーの場合は、お店の方に相談した方がよいです。」— shared cooking equipment and dishware with wheat dishes.
Not explicitly documented whether tamari is used; standard shoyu contains wheat — confirm per dish.
Menu is plant-based/macrobiotic; a few egg items exist (e.g. スパニッシュオムレツ), so vegan guests should confirm per dish.
Site states allergy accommodation is available if requested in advance (アレルギー対応・事前申告).
Roughly one-third of the menu is gluten-free, built on brown rice / rice flour, and empacede rates it ★★★.

name: Menshou Mabushiya Matsumoto (炙り味噌らーめん 麺匠真武咲弥 松本店)

claims.text: GF brown-rice noodles are by default boiled in the same water as wheat noodles unless a separate pot is requested — high cross-contact risk without asking.
Soy-sauce (shoyu) ramen and standard seasonings likely contain wheat; miso base may contain barley — confirm tamari/GF seasoning before ordering.
Oriental vegetarian line exists but broth is not confirmed vegan; shared kitchen with meat and wheat.
Staff will use a separate boiling pot on request and were flexible (e.g. separating the spicy miso condiment) per the blogger.
A dedicated GF brown-rice-noodle ramen and GF karaage are on the regular menu, and staff accommodate a separate-pot request.

GF pizza and pasta are provided only as a paid substitution; the same kitchen makes wheat natural-yeast pizza and durum-wheat fresh pasta, and no dedicated GF prep line, oven or boiling water is documented — cross-contact risk is real.
「ピザとパスタをメインとするレストランで、追加料金でピザとパスタをグルテンフリーにすることができます。」— GF is described as an add-on swap, not a separate celiac-safe kitchen.
No tamari/wheat-free soy statement published; Italian menu, but confirm sauces on the salad bar and any dressings for wheat-based soy or seasonings.
Salad bar lunch is explicitly built to suit both gluten-free and vegan diets with carefully selected seasonings and herbs.
Staff will make pizza/pasta gluten-free on request for an extra charge, indicating willingness to accommodate; degree of cross-contact care is not documented — verify by phone.
★★★★★ top rating in the empacede JP gluten-free guide for making both pizza and pasta GF on request.
Additive-free, organic kitchen using no chemical seasonings and no white sugar, with GF/vegan-friendly salad bar.

Wheat-ramen kitchen — the standard noodle is wheat-and-tapioca and no source confirms a dedicated pot or separate boiling water for the gluten-free noodle. Assume shared-water cross-contact unless staff confirm otherwise.

Broths are built on locally-sourced soy sauce and miso (地産地消) with no published tamari or wheat-free-soy claim; standard broths likely contain wheat via soy sauce. The advertised 小麦不使用 (wheat-free) bowl must be requested explicitly.
Vegan and vegetarian ramen are made in the same kitchen as fish/meat broths; confirm the vegan tare/soup on the day.
Shop explicitly advertises allergy accommodation: 「卵不使用、小麦不使用のアレルギー対策もできます」 (egg-free and wheat-free accommodation possible) and 「グルテンフリーの麺も用意しております」.
MSG-free / additive-free (無化調・無添加) kitchen with a stated 'barrier-free' ethos that welcomes wheat-allergy, egg-allergy and vegan guests — an unusually allergy-aware ramen shop.
Gluten-free noodle available as a standing swap for +¥220.

name: Roots Cafe Hakuba (ルーツカフェ)

claims.text: Small seasonal shared kitchen; pizza and baked goods share a single oven and prep space, creating cross-contact risk. A reviewer noted staff were uncertain which items contained gluten.
Soy 'karaage' is marinated overnight in garlic, salt koji, soy sauce and sake lees — standard soy sauce contains wheat unless tamari is used; verify.
Fully vegan kitchen — no meat, fish, dairy or egg used, so animal cross-contact is not a concern.
GF knowledge appears inconsistent among staff; one visitor reported uncertainty about which items contained gluten.
Explicitly lists gluten-free items (curry, tortilla chips, pancakes) and uses rice flour instead of wheat for baked goods.
100% vegan, organic and locally-grown ingredients.

name: Shinshu Juwari Soba Ten Karuizawa (信州十割そば てん 軽井沢店)

claims.text: 十割そば 「つなぎを一切使わない」 with 打ち粉不使用 (no wheat binder, no wheat dusting flour); soba-only kitchen. Confirm a dedicated boiling pot on arrival — not documented online.
「本店と同じグルテンフリーのつゆ」 — the dipping sauce is stated to be gluten-free (wheat-free), unusual for a soba shop.
Tsuyu is dashi-based (likely bonito); vegetable tempura batter is rice+buckwheat flour — confirm no egg/fish for vegan needs.
Whole GF offering (noodles, tsuyu, tempura) is a deliberate concept, so staff are geared toward gluten-free requests.
「米粉と蕎麦粉を合わせて揚げたグルテンフリーの天ぷら」— gluten-free tempura (rice + buckwheat flour, no wheat), letting celiacs have tempura with the soba.
